bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷三十一 周臣傳第十九: 王朴 鄭仁誨 扈載
title.en: Volume 31 Later Zhou Biographies 11: Wang Pu, Zheng Renhui, Hu Zai
title.raw: 卷三十一 周臣傳第十九: 王朴 鄭仁誨 扈載 Volume 31 Later Zhou Biographies 11: Wang Pu, Zheng Renhui, Hu Zai

sentences.zh: 王朴，字文伯，東平人也。

translations.literal: Wang Pu, styled Wenbo, was a native of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, styled Wenbo, came from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士，為校書郎，依漢樞密使楊邠。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the jinshi examination, became proofreader, and attached himself to Yang Bin, Privy Council commissioner of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi while young, became a proofreader, and served under Yang Bin, Han’s Privy Council commissioner.

sentences.zh: 邠與王章、史弘肇等有隙，朴見漢興日淺，隱帝年少孱弱，任用小人，而邠為大臣，與將相交惡，知其必亂，乃去邠東歸。

translations.literal: Bin had a rift with Wang Zhang, Shi Hongzhao, and others. Pu saw that Han had risen only recently, that the Hidden Emperor was young and weak and employed petty men, and that Bin as a chief minister was at odds with the generals. Knowing chaos must follow, he left Bin and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Bin feuded with Wang Zhang, Shi Hongzhao, and others. Pu saw Han still new, the Hidden Emperor young and frail, petty men in power—and Bin, a chief minister, at war with the generals. He knew ruin was coming and left Bin for the east.

sentences.zh: 後李業等教隱帝誅權臣，邠與章、弘肇皆見殺，三家之客多及，而朴以故獨免。

translations.literal: Later Li Ye and others urged the Hidden Emperor to execute the powerful ministers; Bin, Zhang, and Hongzhao were all killed, and many clients of the three households were implicated—yet Pu alone escaped because of his prior departure.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Ye and others persuaded the Hidden Emperor to purge the powerful ministers. Bin, Zhang, and Hongzhao were killed; clients of all three houses fell with them—Pu alone was spared, having left in time.

sentences.zh: 周世宗鎮澶州，朴為節度掌書記。

translations.literal: When Zhou Shizong governed Chanz, Pu served as the military governor’s chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong of Zhou held Chanz, Pu was the military governor’s chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 世宗為開封尹，拜朴右拾遺，為推官。

translations.literal: When Shizong became Kaifeng Intendant, Pu was appointed Right Reminder and made investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong became Kaifeng Intendant, Pu was made Right Reminder and investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷比部郎中，獻《平邊策》，曰：

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Pu was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and submitted the “Pacifying the Borderlands” memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At Shizong’s accession Pu rose to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and submitted his “Pacifying the Borderlands” memorial:

sentences.zh: 唐失道而失吳、蜀，晉失道而失幽、并。

translations.literal: Tang lost the Way and lost Wu and Shu; Jin lost the Way and lost You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang lost the Way—and with it Wu and Shu. Jin lost the Way—and with it You and Bing.

sentences.zh: 觀所以失之之由，知所以平之之術。

translations.literal: Observe the causes by which they were lost, and you will know the methods by which to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Study why they were lost, and you learn how to win them back.

sentences.zh: 當失之時，君暗政亂，兵驕民困，近者奸於內，遠者叛於外，小不制而至於僭，大不制而至於濫，天下離心，人不用命，吳、蜀乘其亂而竊其號，幽、并乘其間而據其地。

translations.literal: At the time of loss, the ruler was dim and government chaotic; soldiers were arrogant and the people exhausted. Those near grew treacherous within; those far rebelled without. Small matters unchecked led to usurpation; great matters unchecked led to excess. The realm lost heart; men would not obey. Wu and Shu seized the disorder and stole their titles; You and Bing seized the interval and held their lands.
translations.idiomatic: When empires fall, rulers grow blind and rule turns rotten; armies swagger while the people starve. Treason festers at court; rebellion rises on the frontier. Small disorders swell into usurpation; large ones into anarchy. The realm loses faith; commands go unheeded. Wu and Shu ride the chaos and steal imperial titles; You and Bing slip in and seize the soil.

sentences.zh: 平之之術，在乎反唐、晉之失而已。

translations.literal: The method of pacification lies simply in reversing Tang’s and Jin’s failures.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify the borderlands, reverse what Tang and Jin did wrong—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 必先進賢退不肖，以清其時；

translations.literal: First advance the worthy and remove the unworthy, to clarify the age;
translations.idiomatic: First promote the worthy and dismiss the unworthy, and the age grows clear;

sentences.zh: 用能去不能，以審其材；

translations.literal: employ the capable and remove the incapable, to discern talent;
translations.idiomatic: use the able and discard the useless, and talent finds its place;

sentences.zh: 恩信號令，以結其心；

translations.literal: with grace, faith, and command, bind their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: with grace, trust, and clear command, bind hearts to you;

sentences.zh: 賞功罰罪，以盡其力；

translations.literal: reward merit and punish crime, to exhaust their strength;
translations.idiomatic: reward merit and punish wrong, and men give all they have;

sentences.zh: 恭儉節用，以豐其財；

translations.literal: with reverence, thrift, and economy, enrich the treasury;
translations.idiomatic: with reverence, thrift, and restraint, fill the treasury;

sentences.zh: 徭役以時，以阜其民。

translations.literal: levy corvée labor in season, to enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: levy labor in its season, and the people grow rich.

sentences.zh: 俟其倉廩實、器用備、人可用而舉之。

translations.literal: Wait until the granaries are full, equipment ready, and men can be employed—then act.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until granaries brim, arms stand ready, and men answer the call—then strike.

sentences.zh: 彼方之民，知我政化大行，上下同心，力強財足，人安將和，有必取之勢，則知彼情狀者願為之間諜，知彼山川者願為之先導。

translations.literal: When the people yonder know our civilizing rule runs deep, that above and below are of one mind, that strength is great and wealth ample, that soldiers are settled and generals united, and that victory is assured—then those who know their secrets will serve as spies, and those who know their mountains and rivers will serve as guides.
translations.idiomatic: When folk across the border see our rule flourishing, court and camp of one mind, strength and silver in hand, soldiers content and commanders aligned—and know we must prevail—those who know their secrets will spy for us, and those who know their hills and rivers will guide us.

sentences.zh: 彼民與此民之心同，是與天意同；

translations.literal: When their people’s hearts match our people’s hearts, that matches Heaven’s will;
translations.idiomatic: When their people’s hearts align with ours, we align with Heaven;

sentences.zh: 與天意同，則無不成之功。

translations.literal: when one matches Heaven’s will, no achievement fails.
translations.idiomatic: and when Heaven is with you, nothing fails.

sentences.zh: 攻取之道，從易者始。

translations.literal: The way of conquest begins with what is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Conquest begins with the easy target.

sentences.zh: 當今惟吳易圖，東至海，南至江，可撓之地二千里。

translations.literal: Today only Wu is easy to take. East to the sea, south to the river—two thousand li of land open to harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Today only Wu yields easily. East to the sea, south to the Yangzi—two thousand li ripe for raiding.

sentences.zh: 從少備處先撓之，備東則撓西，備西則撓東，彼必奔走以救其弊，奔走之間，可以知彼之虛實、眾之強弱，攻虛擊弱，則所向無前矣。

translations.literal: Begin by harrying where defenses are thin. If they reinforce the east, harry the west; if the west, harry the east. They must rush to save each breach; in that rushing you learn their emptiness and fullness, the strength and weakness of their forces. Strike the empty and hit the weak, and nothing stands before you.
translations.idiomatic: Harass where they are lightly held. Reinforce the east, strike the west; reinforce the west, strike the east. They will scramble to plug every gap—and in the scramble you learn where they are hollow and where they stand firm. Hit the hollow and break the weak, and nothing can stop you.

sentences.zh: 勿大舉，但以輕兵撓之。

translations.literal: Do not launch a great campaign—only send light troops to harass.
translations.idiomatic: Do not mount a full invasion—only light troops to harry and probe.

sentences.zh: 彼人怯弱，知我師入其地，必大發以來應，數大發則民困而國竭，一不大發則我獲其利。

translations.literal: Their people are timid. When they know our armies have entered their land, they must mobilize heavily to respond. Repeated heavy mobilization exhausts the people and drains the state; one failure to mobilize and we take the profit.
translations.idiomatic: They are a timid people. Once our columns cross their border, they must raise great armies to meet us. Raise them again and again, and the people break and the treasury empties; fail to raise them once, and the gain is ours.

sentences.zh: 彼竭我利，則江北諸州乃國家之所有也。

translations.literal: When they are exhausted and we profit, the northern-bank prefectures north of the river become the state’s own.
translations.idiomatic: They spent, we enriched—then the Yangzi’s north-bank prefectures are ours.

sentences.zh: 既得江北，則用彼之民，揚我之兵，江之南亦不難而平之也。

translations.literal: Once the north bank is taken, use their people and raise our banners—the south bank is not hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the north bank, draft their people, march our banners south—and the river’s southern shore falls without great trouble.

sentences.zh: 如此，則用力少而收功多。

translations.literal: Thus little effort yields great reward.
translations.idiomatic: So: little force, great gain.

sentences.zh: 得吳，則桂、廣皆為內臣，岷、蜀可飛書而召之。

translations.literal: Once Wu is taken, Gui and Guang become inner subjects; Min and Shu can be summoned by a flying dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Take Wu, and Guangxi and Guangdong bow inward; Min and Shu can be called by a single urgent letter.

sentences.zh: 如不至，則四面並進，席卷而蜀平矣。

translations.literal: If they do not come, advance on every side and sweep Shu flat in one roll.
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse, advance on every front and roll Shu up in one sweep.

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀平，幽可望風而至。

translations.literal: When Wu and Shu are pacified, You may come at the wind’s turning.
translations.idiomatic: Pacify Wu and Shu, and You may submit at the first rumor of your approach.

sentences.zh: 唯并必死之寇，不可以恩信誘，必須以強兵攻，力已竭，氣已喪，不足以為邊患，可為後圖。

translations.literal: Only Bing is a foe that will fight to the death; it cannot be lured by grace and faith. It must be taken by strong armies. Once its strength is spent and its spirit broken, it will not suffice as a border threat and can be left for later.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bing is an enemy that dies fighting; grace and promises will not move it. Strong armies must break it. Once its strength is gone and its nerve shattered, it ceases to threaten the frontier—and can wait.

sentences.zh: 方今兵力精練，器用具備，群下知法，諸將用命，一稔之後，可以平邊。

translations.literal: Today the armies are honed, equipment complete, subordinates know the law, and generals obey—after one full harvest, the borderlands can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Today the troops are sharp, the arsenals full, the court knows law, and the generals obey. One year from now, the borderlands can be settled.

sentences.zh: 臣書生也，不足以講大事，至於不達大體，不合機變，惟陛下寬之。

translations.literal: Your servant is a mere scholar, unfit to discuss great affairs; should I miss the larger pattern or fail to suit changing circumstance, may Your Majesty be indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a bookish man, unqualified to speak of great strategy. If I miss the larger design or fail the moment’s need, I beg Your Majesty’s forbearance.

sentences.zh: 遷左諫議大夫，知開封府事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Remonstrance Councillor and made administrator of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Remonstrance Councillor and took charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 歲中，遷左散騎常侍，充端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Within the year he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant and made Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he became Left Regular Attendant and Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness.

sentences.zh: 是時，世宗新即位，銳意征伐，已撓群議，親敗劉旻於高平，歸而益治兵，慨然有平一天下之志。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong had newly acceded, was keen on campaigns, had already overborne collective opinion, had personally defeated Liu Min at Gaoping, and on returning further drilled the armies—suddenly possessed of the will to pacify all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had just taken the throne, hungry for war. He had already silenced the doubters, beaten Liu Min at Gaoping himself, and returned to drill the armies harder—suddenly burning to unite the realm.

sentences.zh: 數顧大臣問治道，選文學之士徐臺符等二十人，使作《為君難為臣不易論》及《平邊策》，朴在選中。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he turned to his ministers to ask the way of governance, selected twenty literary men including Xu Taifu, and had them compose “On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister” and “Pacifying the Borderlands”—Pu was among those chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he asked his ministers how to rule. He picked twenty literary men, Xu Taifu among them, and set them to write “On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister” and “Pacifying the Borderlands”—Pu was chosen.

sentences.zh: 而當時文士皆不欲上急於用武，以謂平定僭亂，在修文德以為先。

translations.literal: Yet the literati of the time did not wish the throne to rush into war, holding that to settle usurpation and disorder one must first cultivate civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Most literati of the day did not want the throne to hurry into war. Usurpation, they said, yields only to civil virtue first.

sentences.zh: 惟翰林學士陶谷竇儀、御史中丞楊昭儉與朴皆言用兵之策，朴謂江淮為可先取。

translations.literal: Only Hanlin Academician Tao Gu, Dou Yi, Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, and Pu all spoke of military strategy; Pu said the Jianghuai could be taken first.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hanlin Academician Tao Gu, Dou Yi, Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, and Pu argued for war—and Pu said take the Jianghuai first.

sentences.zh: 世宗雅已知朴，及見其議論偉然，益以為奇，引與計議天下事，無不合，遂決意用之。

translations.literal: Shizong had long known Pu; when he saw his discourse so bold, he thought him even more remarkable, drew him into planning the realm’s affairs—nothing failed to agree—and resolved to employ him fully.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had known Pu for years; now his arguments struck like thunder, and Shizong found him even more extraordinary. He brought Pu into every plan for the realm. Nothing clashed. He decided to use him without reserve.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，征淮，以仆為東京副留守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande, during the Huai campaign, Pu was made Deputy Commissioner of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiande year three, on the Huai campaign, Pu was made Deputy Commissioner of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 還，拜戶部侍郎、樞密副使，遷樞密使。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Deputy Privy Council Commissioner, then promoted to Privy Council Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Back from the field he became Vice Minister of Revenue and Deputy Privy Council Commissioner, then Privy Council Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，再征淮，以朴留守京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the second Huai campaign, Pu was left to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, on the second Huai campaign, Pu stayed behind to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗之時，外事征伐，而內修法度。

translations.literal: In Shizong’s time, foreign affairs meant campaigns while domestic affairs meant repairing law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, war ran outward and law was rebuilt within.

sentences.zh: 朴為人明敏多材智，非獨當世之務，至於陰陽律歷之法，莫不通焉。

translations.literal: Pu was bright, keen, and rich in talent—not only in affairs of the age; in yin-yang, pitch pipes, and calendrics he had no branch he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was quick, brilliant, and many-sided—not only in the business of the day. Yin and yang, pitch pipes, calendrics: there was no art he did not command.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年，詔朴校定大歷，乃削去近世符天流俗不經之學，設通、經、統三法，以歲軌離交朔望周變率策之數，步日月五星，為《欽天曆》。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande, an edict ordered Pu to revise the Great Calendar. He cut away recent Futian and vulgar, unorthodox learning, established three methods—comprehensive, canonical, and systematic—and from the numbers of the year’s track, lunar nodes, new and full moons, cyclical changes, rates, and procedures calculated sun, moon, and the five planets, producing the Qintian Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Xiande year two, an edict put Pu to revising the Great Calendar. He stripped out recent Futian astrology and folk superstition, set up three methods—comprehensive, canonical, and systematic—and from the year’s track, lunar nodes, new and full moons, cyclical shifts, rates, and procedures calculated sun, moon, and the five planets, producing the Qintian Calendar.

sentences.zh: 六年，又詔朴考正雅樂，朴以謂十二律管互吹，難得其真，乃依京房為律準，以九尺之弦十三，依管長短寸分設柱，用七聲為均，樂成而和。

translations.literal: In the sixth year another edict ordered Pu to rectify court music. Pu held that when the twelve pitch pipes blow against one another, the true pitch is hard to obtain; he therefore followed Jing Fang’s pitch standard, set thirteen strings of nine feet, placed bridges according to each pipe’s length in inches and fractions, used the seven tones as the mean—and the music, once complete, was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Year six brought another edict: rectify court music. Pu argued that cross-blowing the twelve pitch pipes never yields true pitch. Following Jing Fang, he built a pitch standard, strung thirteen nine-foot strings, set bridges to each pipe’s length in inches and fractions, tuned to the seven-tone scale—and the music, finished, rang true.

sentences.zh: 朴性剛果，又見信於世宗，凡其所為，當時無敢難者，然人亦莫能加也。

translations.literal: Pu’s nature was firm and decisive, and Shizong trusted him; whatever he did, none in his day dared oppose him—yet none could surpass him either.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was hard and decisive, and Shizong believed in him. Whatever he undertook, no one dared stand in his way—nor could anyone outdo him.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮，朴留京師，廣新城，通道路，莊偉宏闊，今京師之制，多其所規為。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned on the Huai, Pu remained at the capital, expanded the new city, opened roads—grand, vast, and broad. Much of the capital’s present layout was his design.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizong fought on the Huai, Pu stayed in the capital, widened the new city, opened roads—monumental and vast. Much of today’s capital plan is his work.

sentences.zh: 其所作樂，至今用之不可變。

translations.literal: The music he made is still used today and cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The music he made is still used today—and cannot be altered.

sentences.zh: 其陳用兵之略，非特一時之策。

translations.literal: The military strategy he laid out was not a plan for one season only.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy he laid out was not a plan for one season alone.

sentences.zh: 至言諸國興滅次第云：「淮南可最先取，並必死之寇，最後亡。

translations.literal: He even spoke of the order in which states would rise and fall: “Huainan can be taken first; Bing, the foe that fights to the death, will perish last.
translations.idiomatic: He even named the order of rise and fall: “Take Huainan first. Bing—the enemy that dies fighting—falls last.

sentences.zh: 」其後宋興，平定四方，惟並獨後服，皆如朴言。

translations.literal: ” Later when Song rose and pacified the four quarters, only Bing submitted last—all as Pu had said.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Song rose and settled the four quarters, only Bing submitted last—exactly as Pu foretold.

sentences.zh: 六年春，世宗遣朴行視汴口，作斗門，還，過故相李穀第，疾作，仆於坐上，舁歸而卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year Shizong sent Pu to inspect the Bian mouth and build sluice gates. Returning, he passed the mansion of the former chancellor Li Gu; illness seized him, he collapsed in his seat, was carried home, and died—aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of year six, Shizong sent Pu to inspect the Bian mouth and build sluice gates. On the way back he stopped at former chancellor Li Gu’s house; sickness took him, he fell from his seat, was carried home, and died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨其喪，以玉鉞叩地，大慟者數四。

translations.literal: Shizong attended his funeral, struck the ground with a jade axe-symbol, and wailed greatly four times.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong came to his funeral, struck the ground with the jade axe of mourning, and broke into great wailing four times.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 鄭仁誨

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui

sentences.zh: 鄭仁誨，字日新，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui, styled Rixin, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui, styled Rixin, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，事唐將陳紹光。

translations.literal: At first he served the Tang general Chen Shaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Tang general Chen Shaoguang.

sentences.zh: 紹光為人驍勇而好使酒，嘗因醉怒仁誨，拔劍欲殺之，左右皆奔走，仁誨植立不動，無懼色，紹光擲劍於地，撫仁誨曰：「汝有器量，必富貴，非吾所及也。

translations.literal: Shaoguang was fierce and brave and loved his wine. Once, drunk and angry at Renhui, he drew his sword to kill him. Those around all fled; Renhui stood rooted, unmoving, without fear. Shaoguang threw his sword to the ground, stroked Renhui, and said: “You have breadth of character—you will surely be rich and noble; that is not within my reach.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoguang was a fierce drinker. Once, drunk and furious at Renhui, he drew his sword to kill him. Everyone fled; Renhui stood still, unafraid. Shaoguang flung down his sword, clapped Renhui’s shoulder, and said: “You have the measure of a great man—you will rise high. That is beyond me.

sentences.zh: 」仁誨後棄紹光去，還鄉里，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: ” Renhui later abandoned Shaoguang, returned to his home district, and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: ” Renhui later left Shaoguang, went home, and became known for honoring his mother.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖為河東節度使，周太祖居帳下，時時往過仁誨，與語甚歡。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu was military governor of Hedong, Zhou Taizu served under his banner and often visited Renhui; their talk was very pleasant.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu governed Hedong, Zhou Taizu served in his camp and often called on Renhui—they talked as old friends.

sentences.zh: 每事有疑，即從仁誨質問，仁誨所對不阿，周太祖益奇之。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizu doubted a matter he would go straight to Renhui to question him; Renhui’s answers did not flatter, and Taizu admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was uncertain, he went to Renhui for plain answers. Renhui never flattered—and Taizu prized him the more.

sentences.zh: 漢興，周太祖為樞密使，乃召仁誨用之，累官至內客省使。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Zhou Taizu became Privy Council Commissioner and summoned Renhui to serve; he rose by degrees to Commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Han was established, Taizu became Privy Council Commissioner and brought Renhui in; he rose step by step to Commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau.

sentences.zh: 太祖破李守貞於河中，軍中機畫，仁誨多所參決。

translations.literal: When Taizu broke Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Renhui took part in many of the army’s strategic decisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu broke Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Renhui helped decide much of the army’s strategy.

sentences.zh: 太祖入立，以仁誨為大內都點檢、恩州團練使、樞密副使，累遷宣徽北院使，出為鎮寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne, he made Renhui Grand Inspector of the Inner Palace, Military Training Commissioner of Enzhou, and Deputy Privy Council Commissioner; he was promoted by degrees to Commissioner of the Northern Hall of the Palace Secretariat, then went out as military governor of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he made Renhui Grand Inspector of the Inner Palace, Military Training Commissioner of Enzhou, and Deputy Privy Council Commissioner; he rose to Commissioner of the Northern Hall of the Palace Secretariat, then went out to govern the Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was made Privy Council Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiande year one, he became Privy Council Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世宗攻河東，仁誨留守東都。

translations.literal: When Shizong attacked Hedong, Renhui remained to hold the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong attacked Hedong, Renhui stayed behind to hold the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，以疾卒。

translations.literal: The next winter he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 世宗將臨其喪，有司言歲不利臨喪，世宗不聽，乃先以桃荝而臨之。

translations.literal: Shizong meant to attend his funeral; the officials said the year was unfavorable for attending funerals. Shizong would not listen and first performed the peach-branch and reed rite before going to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong meant to attend his funeral; the officials warned that the year was ill-omened for mourning. Shizong refused to heed them, performed the peach-branch and reed exorcism, and went anyway.

sentences.zh: 仁誨自其微時，常為太祖謀畫，及居大位，未嘗有所聞，而太祖、世宗皆親重之，然亦能謙謹好禮，不自矜伐，為士大夫所稱。

translations.literal: From his humble days Renhui had often plotted for Taizu; once in high office nothing was ever heard of him—yet Taizu and Shizong both held him in personal esteem. He was also humble, courteous, and fond of ritual, never boasting of himself, and the literati praised him.
translations.idiomatic: From humble days Renhui had advised Taizu; in high office he never traded on it—yet Taizu and Shizong both cherished him. He remained modest, courteous, and ritual-minded, never vaunting himself, and the literati spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，追封韓國公，謚曰忠正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Councillor, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Han, and given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Councillor, enfeoffed as Duke of Han, and given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 扈載，字仲熙，北燕人也。

translations.literal: Hu Zai, styled Zhongxi, was a native of Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zai, styled Zhongxi, came from Northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved books and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，舉進士高第，拜校書郎，直史館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he passed the jinshi with high rank, was appointed proofreader, and served directly in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he took the jinshi with top honors, became proofreader, and served in the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 再遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 其為文章，以辭多自喜。

translations.literal: In his writing he took pride in ornate language.
translations.idiomatic: In his prose he took pride in rich language.

sentences.zh: 常次歷代有國廢興治亂之跡為《運源賦》，甚詳。

translations.literal: He once compiled the traces of dynastic rise, fall, order, and disorder through the ages into “Origins of Fate,” in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the rise, fall, order, and chaos of dynasties through the ages into “Origins of Fate”—a work of great detail.

sentences.zh: 又因遊相國寺，見庭竹可愛，作《碧鮮賦》，題其壁，世宗聞之，遣小黃門就壁錄之，覽而稱善，因拜水部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Also, while visiting Xiangguo Temple he saw courtyard bamboo he loved and wrote “Fresh Green,” inscribing it on the wall. Shizong heard of it, sent a palace eunuch to copy it from the wall, read it and praised it, and therefore appointed him Vice Director of the Waterways Office and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Xiangguo Temple, he fell in love with the courtyard bamboo and wrote “Fresh Green” on the wall. Shizong heard, sent a palace eunuch to copy it from the wall, read it with praise, and made him Vice Director of the Waterways Office and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士，賜緋，而載已病，不能朝謝。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician and granted crimson robes—but Zai was already ill and could not attend court to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin Academician and was granted crimson robes—but Zai was already ill and could not attend court to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 居百餘日，乃力疾入直學士院。

translations.literal: After more than a hundred days he forced himself, ill, to enter duty at the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred days he dragged himself, sick, into duty at the Academy.

sentences.zh: 世宗憐之，賜告還第，遣太醫視疾。

translations.literal: Shizong took pity on him, granted leave to return home, and sent the imperial physician to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong pitied him, granted leave to go home, and sent the imperial physician to treat him.

sentences.zh: 初，載以文知名一時，樞密使王朴尤重其才，薦於宰相李穀，久而不用，朴以問穀曰：「扈載不為舍人，何也？

translations.literal: At first, when Zai was famous in his day for letters, Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu especially valued his talent and recommended him to Chancellor Li Gu. Long he was not employed. Pu asked Gu: “Why is Hu Zai not made Drafting Secretary?
translations.idiomatic: When Zai was famous for his writing, Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu especially prized his talent and recommended him to Chancellor Li Gu—but Gu would not use him. Pu asked Gu: “Why is Hu Zai not made Drafting Secretary?

sentences.zh: 」穀曰：「非不知其才，然載命薄，恐不能勝。

translations.literal: ” Gu said: “It is not that I do not know his talent—but Zai’s fate is thin; I fear he cannot bear the office.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gu said: “I know his talent. But Zai’s fate is thin—I fear the office would break him.

sentences.zh: 」朴曰：「公為宰相，以進賢退不肖為職，何言命邪？

translations.literal: ” Pu said: “You are chancellor; advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy is your charge—why speak of fate?
translations.idiomatic: ” Pu said: “You are chancellor. Promoting the worthy and dismissing the unworthy is your duty—why talk of fate?

sentences.zh: 」已而召拜知制誥。

translations.literal: ” Soon after, Zai was summoned and appointed drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon after, Zai was summoned and made drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 及為學士，居歲中病卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: Once he became Academician, within the year he died of illness—aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Once Academician, he died of illness within the year—thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 議者以穀能知人而朴能薦士。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Gu could know men and Pu could recommend talent.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said Gu knew men—and Pu knew how to recommend them.

sentences.zh: 是時，天子英武，樂延天下奇才，而尤禮文士，載與張昭、竇儼、陶穀、徐臺符等俱被進用。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was heroic and martial, delighted to gather the realm’s extraordinary men, and especially honored literati. Zai, together with Zhang Zhao, Dou Yan, Tao Gu, Xu Taifu, and others, were all promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven was bold and martial, hungry for extraordinary men, and especially honored men of letters. Zai, with Zhang Zhao, Dou Yan, Tao Gu, Xu Taifu, and others, all rose into office.

sentences.zh: 穀居數人中，文辭最劣，尤無行。

translations.literal: Among those several men, Gu’s literary skill was the worst—and his conduct especially lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Among them Gu wrote worst—and behaved worst.

sentences.zh: 昭、儼數與論議，其文粲然，而穀徒能先意所在，以進諛取合人主，事無大小，必稱美頌贊，至於廣京城，為木偶耕人、紫芝白兔之類，皆為頌以獻，其辭大抵類俳優。

translations.literal: Zhao and Yan often debated with him; their writing blazed—but Gu could only anticipate the ruler’s mind, advance flattery to win favor, and on matters large or small always offer praise and eulogy. Even widening the capital city, wooden farm figures, purple fungus, white hares—all received his celebratory odes, his words mostly like a jester’s.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Yan often argued with him; their prose shone. Gu could only read the ruler’s mood, flatter ahead of it, and praise every deed, great or small. Widening the capital, wooden farm figures, purple fungus, white hares—all won his hymns of praise, his words mostly fit for a clown.

sentences.zh: 而載以不幸早卒，論議雖不及昭、儼，而不為穀之諛也。

translations.literal: Zai, through misfortune, died young; in debate he did not reach Zhao and Yan—yet he did not flatter as Gu did.
translations.idiomatic: Zai, cut off young, never matched Zhao and Yan in argument—but he never flattered like Gu.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 作器者，無良材而有良匠；

translations.literal: To make vessels, one needs no fine timber but a fine craftsman;
translations.idiomatic: To shape a vessel you need no perfect timber—only a perfect craftsman;

sentences.zh: 治國者，無能臣而有能君。

translations.literal: to govern a state, one needs no able ministers but an able ruler.
translations.idiomatic: to govern a state you need no perfect ministers—only a perfect ruler.

sentences.zh: 蓋材待匠而成，臣待君而用。

translations.literal: Timber waits on the craftsman to be made; ministers wait on the ruler to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Timber waits for the craftsman; ministers wait for the ruler.

sentences.zh: 故曰，治國譬之於奕，知其用而置得其處者勝，不知其用而置非其處者敗。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: governing the state is like a game of Go—knowing how to use men and placing each in his proper place wins; not knowing how to use men and placing each where he does not belong loses.
translations.idiomatic: So they say: governing a state is like Go—know your pieces and place each where it belongs, and you win; misplace them, and you lose.

sentences.zh: 敗者臨棋註目，終日而勞心，使善奕者視焉，為之易置其處則勝矣。

translations.literal: The loser stares at the board all day, laboring in mind; let a skilled player look—and by rearranging the pieces to their proper places, victory follows.
translations.idiomatic: The loser stares at the board all day, mind in knots; let a master look—and by moving each piece to its right square, the game turns.

sentences.zh: 勝者所用，敗者之棋也；

translations.literal: What the victor uses are the loser’s chess stones;
translations.idiomatic: The stones the victor plays are the loser’s own pieces.

sentences.zh: 興國所用，亡國之臣也。

translations.literal: What a rising state uses are the ministers of a perished state.
translations.idiomatic: The men a rising realm employs are the ministers of a fallen one.

sentences.zh: 王朴之材，誠可謂能矣。

translations.literal: Wang Pu’s talents may truly be called capable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu’s talent was genuine—capable indeed.

sentences.zh: 不遇世宗，何所施哉？

translations.literal: Had he not met Shizong, where would he have applied them?
translations.idiomatic: Without Shizong, where could he have shown it?

sentences.zh: 世宗之時，外事征伐，攻取戰勝；

translations.literal: In Shizong’s time, outwardly there was campaigning—in attack and conquest, victory in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong the realm campaigned abroad—attacking, conquering, winning in battle;

sentences.zh: 內修制度，議刑法，定律歷，講求禮樂之遺文，所用者五代之士也，豈皆愚怯於晉、漢，而材智於周哉？

translations.literal: inwardly he refined institutions, debated penal law, fixed calendar and statutes, and sought out surviving texts of rites and music—the men he employed were men of the Five Dynasties; were they all stupid and timid under Jin and Han, yet talented and wise under Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: Within he refined institutions, debated law, fixed the calendar, and recovered lost rites and music—the men he used were veterans of the Five Dynasties. Were they fools and cowards under Jin and Han, yet sages under Zhou?

sentences.zh: 惟知所用爾。

translations.literal: It is only a matter of knowing whom to employ.
translations.idiomatic: It comes down to knowing whom to use.

sentences.zh: 夫亂國之君，常置愚不肖於上，而強其不能，以暴其短惡，置賢智於下，而泯沒其材能，使君子、小人皆失其所，而身蹈危亡。

translations.literal: A ruler who disorders his state commonly sets the foolish and unworthy above, forcing them beyond what they can do to expose their faults and vices; sets the wise and talented below, burying their abilities, so that gentlemen and petty men alike lose their proper place—and he himself walks into danger and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who brings ruin puts fools in high office and drives them beyond their strength until their flaws stand bare; puts the wise below and buries their gifts, so gentlemen and petty men alike lose their proper stations—and he himself walks into peril and extinction.

sentences.zh: 治國之君，能置賢智於近，而置愚不肖於遠，使君子、小人各適其分，而身享安榮。

translations.literal: A ruler who orders his state can set the wise and talented near and the foolish and unworthy far, so gentlemen and petty men each fit their rank—and he himself enjoys safety and glory.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who brings order keeps the wise close and the unworthy far, so gentlemen and petty men each fill their proper roles—and he enjoys safety and honor himself.

sentences.zh: 治亂相去雖遠甚，而其所以致之者不多也，反其所置而已。

translations.literal: Though order and disorder stand vastly far apart, the causes that lead to them are not many—it is simply reversing whom one places where.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder seem worlds apart, yet what makes them differ is small: simply reverse whom you place where.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，自古治君少而亂君多，況於五代，士之遇不遇者，可勝嘆哉！

translations.literal: Alas! From antiquity there have been few ordering rulers and many disordered ones; how much the more in the Five Dynasties—the scholars who found favor and those who did not, what sighs could number them all!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! Through the ages worthy rulers have been rare and ruinous ones many—all the more in the Five Dynasties. How many scholars found a master, and how many did not—what sighs could count them all!
